cues: A whole yak… in one winter?!
I'm Seetu, eating through every district of India.
Stop two: Changthang, land of nomad herders.
Breakfast: tsampa, roasted barley flour, stirred into salty butter tea.
Lunch, in many nomad homes, is meat and dairy:
yak or mutton stew, and churpe, dried cheese.
Ow! Okay… you soften it in tea.
Dinner? Like much of Ladakh: thukpa, warm noodle soup.
Mind blown: researchers found a nomad family may eat one yak, or three to four sheep or goats, each winter.
And these herders are among India's top pashmina producers: cashmere wool!
